subject: Recap: Aurelia Health discovery — private hosting constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@aureliahealth.com>, Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Aurelia Health discovery — private hosting constraints & next steps

Hi Samir / Rachel — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we all have a shared view and clear next steps. Please correct anything I get wrong.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Primary driver: regulatory requirement to keep patient data within their VPC and block persistent outbound connections to third-party endpoints (state-level data residency + audit requirements).
- Secondary: strict change-control windows (maintenance only during weekends), need for hardware-backed key storage (HSM/KMS control), and detailed audit logs for token-level access.
- Outcome desired: a hosted inference solution deployed into Aurelia's VPC or fully air-gapped on-prem package that meets SOC2-like evidence and lets product teams call endpoints over a private network.

Key constraints we agreed on
- No egress to the public internet from inference hosts; only approved internal destinations.
- TLS termination inside customer network; Redwood must support mutual TLS or private endpoint with customer-provided certs.
- HV swap windows: 2am–6am local (weekends only) — we need maintenance plan aligned to this.
- HSM/KMS requirement: customer will provide HSM or integrate with an on-prem KMS with PKCS#11.

Risks & open questions
- Network topology: is VPC peering allowed, or must we run an isolated subnet with private endpoints? (Samir noted peering preferred but needs security sign-off.)
- Audit log retention: Aurelia needs 7 years for certain records — will need to confirm storage/retention mechanism.
- Remote patching: how will emergency security patches be applied in an air-gapped setup?

Proposed next steps (owner — due dates)
1) Aurelia: return the completed network questionnaire (attached) with firewall rules and approved egress destinations — due Tue 2028-04-05 — Samir / Rachel.
2) Redwood (SE): produce an architecture sketch showing 1) VPC peering option and 2) isolated private endpoint + jump-host flow — Ben — due Fri 2028-04-06.
3) Security deep-dive: schedule a 60-min call between Aurelia security, Ben (SE), and Laura (solutions) to review KMS/HSM integration and logging — target week of 4/9 — Tessa to coordinate.
4) Legal/Procurement: we'll surface the standard SOW template for an on-prem deployment and a redline-friendly commercial brief — Tessa/Laura — initial draft by 4/13.

Attachments I uploaded: filled questionnaire (please fill gaps), call recording, short Redwood private hosting brief.

If that matches your sense, I’ll pull together calendar options for the security deep-dive and loop in our engineering lead for the technical dive. Thanks again — appreciated the clarity on the residency requirement.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Aurelia_Network_Questionnaire.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: call-recording-2028-04-02.mp3 (audio)
Attachment: redwood-private-hosting-highlevel.pdf (pdf)

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@aureliahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Aurelia Health discovery — private hosting constraints & next steps

Thanks Tessa — this looks right. A couple clarifications from our side:
- We can do VPC peering in production but the peering request must be approved by network ops (2–3 week lead). For the POC we prefer an isolated private endpoint behind our NAT.
- HSM: we have an on-prem Thales HSM that supports PKCS#11; Rachel will share the admin contact and cert requirements in the questionnaire.
- Audit retention: 7 years is correct for a subset of audit records; we can start with 90-day logs for the POC and extend once retention tooling is validated.

I’ve attached a partially completed questionnaire. I’ll aim to have the rest by EOD Tue 4/5. Also, security@aureliahealth.com will join the deep-dive call.

—Samir
Samir Gupta
Director, Platform Engineering | Aurelia Health
Attachment: Aurelia_Network_Questionnaire_partially_completed.pdf (pdf)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Perfect, Samir — thanks for confirming. Looping in Ben and Laura to pick up the technical architecture and SOW drafting: Ben — can you produce the two sketches (peering vs isolated endpoint) and a short feasibility note about integrating with a Thales HSM (PKCS#11)? Laura — can you surface the on-prem SOW template and list the standard air-gap exclusions we’ve seen historically?

Proposed calendar for the security deep-dive (choose one):
- Thu 2028-04-11 10:00–11:00 PT
- Tue 2028-04-16 16:00–17:00 PT

If those don’t work I’ll send some additional times. Thanks all.

Tessa

On a process note: Samir, if your procurement team prefers a short 1-pager commercial brief before the full SOW, we can produce that same week (4/9–4/13).

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@aureliahealth.com>, Rachel Lim <rachel.lim@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Aurelia Health discovery — private hosting constraints & next steps

Thanks Tessa / Samir — I’ll take the architecture sketches and a short note on Thales HSM support. Quick answers up front:
- VPC peering path: straightforward, expect NAT rules for egress control and a secure private endpoint. Latency should be low; typical tokens/sec targets are achievable with a small dedicated pool.
- Isolated endpoint path: requires a jump host or reverse-proxy inside the customer subnet; we’ll need one inbound rule to allow the Redwood orchestration component to pull images / updates during maintenance windows, or we can provide an offline image + manual update process for true air-gap.
- HSM: PKCS#11 is supported for key wrapping; we’ll confirm exact driver compatibility and list of supported firmware versions in the feasibility note.

I’ll share the sketches and feasibility note by EOD Fri 2028-04-06 and propose a tech-deep-dive slot for Thu 2028-04-11 if that works for your security team.

–Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
